songs.title: Free Air
songs.verdict: A floaty plugg single from St. Petersburg where the mood and the video carry more than the bars.
songs.body:
Sir Soylok is a Kurgan-born rapper now based in Saint Petersburg, working the hazier end of the Russian plugg and pluggnb underground. “Free Air” is a standalone single with a video, tagged ambient plugg, cloud rap and alt R&B.

**Production:** Gustavio Topman composed and produced it, with aprilveahcu and saig credited as features. **Vocals & delivery:** Sir Soylok wrote and performs it; no source describes his delivery in detail. **Melody & hook:** the tags point to atmosphere over punch. The one write-up so far mostly praised the video’s visuals.

Replay will come down to whether the haze holds up without the visuals. The limit: coverage is a single curator mention, so this is a lane read more than a verdict.
songs.scout_note: Rap lane (international plugg). ~14K Spotify monthly listeners. Out Oct 23, 2026 per Spotify. Covered in Erik Pérou's Weekly Wrap Up Oct 19-25: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-oct-19th-2026-oct. Spotify verified by fetch. Source also lists YouTube _5pQ0TAC2Sk and SoundCloud, not verified.

songs.title: FACE
songs.verdict: A two-minute jolt of glitchy, house-driven pop rap from a one-man operation that sounds like nobody else in rap right now.
songs.body:
CONNIE is a Rockford, Illinois-born, LA-based artist who makes almost everything himself, from the production and mix to the master, cover art and editing. “FACE” (2:03) is pop rap pulled toward the club: electro, fidget house and glitch hop sit under the rap.

**Production** is the hook: the tags point to fidget-house bounce and glitchy edits rather than trap drums. **Vocals & delivery:** a pop-rap performance; the details are for the listen. **Melody & hook:** at two minutes it has to hit fast. The AI-assisted video is part of the package, and the idontknowerik newsletter calls his use of it one of the rare ones that adds to the mood.

The same writer calls his music unhinged and bizarre in a way that somehow works, and that's the honest summary: replay depends on whether the chaos lands for you. Short runtime helps; if it doesn't click, there's nothing to settle into.
songs.scout_note: Rap lane, leans club. ~78K Spotify monthly listeners (under the cutoff but the biggest rap pick). Out Oct 5, 2026. Source: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-sept-28th-2026-oct. Spotify verified by fetch.

songs.title: A GOOD AND LONG TIME
songs.verdict: A South London rapper-producer bets on range across 15 tracks, from UK drill to afro trap, with plenty of guests.
songs.body:
N4T is a 22-year-old South London rapper-producer of Ghanaian and Jamaican heritage, part of the scene around Jim Legxacy that Dazed framed as a renaissance in Black British music. His 2025 album GHANAMUSTGO was tagged nu-Afropop; this follow-up, out Oct 16, runs 15 tracks, and he previewed it as a two-sided record, party first, then a love letter to his home city.

**Production:** he's credited with production and mixing himself, which keeps a single hand on a wide spread of UK drill, afro trap and conscious rap. **Vocals & delivery:** a long guest list shares the mic. **Lyrics:** identity and heritage have been his throughline.

The ambition is clear and the scene cosign is real, but there's no critical write-up of the album yet. The risk with 15 tracks across this many lanes: range can read as no center.
songs.scout_note: Rap lane (UK). ~34K Spotify monthly listeners. Out Oct 16, 2026. Source: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-oct-12th-2026-oct. Entered as album since no standout track was named. Spotify album verified by fetch.

songs.title: Forever An Angel
songs.verdict: Fifteen tracks of plugg, rage and glitchy digicore, almost all of it made by one person.
songs.body:
uziellsiilver has been releasing plugg, pluggnb and cloud rap since 2023 and sits around 24K monthly listeners. Forever An Angel, out Oct 16, is 15 tracks with guests including shxrda and leahsdeathbed, and it was singled out in a roundup on the current underground scene.

**Production:** he handles composition, production, programming and synths himself; tags run from pluggnb and rage to digicore, jerk, hardstyle and reggaetón, which says a lot about range and nothing yet about cohesion. **Vocals & delivery:** also his, alongside a guest list of bytt, death souljah, dj megan23, pcyy and yohei. Standouts: the title track and “rawr xd”, the two with videos.

The knock is length: 15 tracks across that many styles is a lot to hold together, and coverage so far is a listing, not a review.
songs.scout_note: Rap/digicore crossover. ~24K Spotify monthly listeners. Out Oct 16, 2026 (Spotify fetched). Source: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-oct-26th-2026-nov, which names the title track and 'rawr xd' as standouts. Two scouts disagreed on hometown (Mexico vs Atlanta), so it's left out of the body; check. Apple/SoundCloud links unverified, left blank.

songs.title: 我只想當個Swagger (I Just Wanna Be Swagger)
songs.verdict: A self-made Chengdu rage-and-jerk record that grabs drill, plugg and hyperpop and makes them sound like home turf.
songs.body:
Siky Revange is a rapper from Chengdu working in rage, plugg, pluggnb and jerk, lanes usually tied to US and UK scenes. I Just Wanna Be Swagger runs 11 tracks and pulls in Chicago drill, trap, hyperpop and dance-pop touches. The one curator write-up so far calls it futuristic swag and is openly a fan.

**Production:** he handles writing, recording, mixing and mastering himself, so the record’s sound is his own call from start to finish. **Vocals & delivery:** he leads, with a long guest list that includes Acid Souljah on “bbb.” **Melody & hook:** “bbb” and “trap music” are the tracks curators point to first, along with video singles like “flexin’ jackie chan.”

For fans of the global rage wave it’s a fresh angle worth digging into. The knock: genre-hopping across 11 tracks can blur, and the buzz so far comes from a small circle of niche curators.
songs.scout_note: Rap lane (China). Very small: ~8.6K Spotify monthly listeners. Out Oct 24, 2026. Sources: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-oct-19th-2026-oct and the Oct 12 wrap-up. Standouts named there: 'bbb', 'trap music'. Buzz is mostly niche curator circles. Spotify verified by fetch.

songs.title: Just Passin' Thru
songs.verdict: Thirteen tracks of no-frills Florida trap with plugg touches: a regional tape that aims to bang and not much else.
songs.body:
509 BMG is an underground rap act from Orlando, Florida, small even by this list's standards. Just Passin' Thru is a 13-track project of dirty-south trap and hardcore rap with plugg edges, out Oct 19.

**Production** comes from a long list of collaborators, including names like evilgiane and kemikelex, which points to the plugg and underground-trap circuit. **Vocals & delivery** and **Lyrics:** 509 BMG is credited for writing and performing; how the verses hold up is for the listen. **Melody & hook:** this is a lane where beat choice does a lot of the work.

The idontknowerik write-up praises it as a simple pleasure: good trap, nothing more needed. That is the ceiling and the knock at once. Thirteen tracks with little documented variety may run together for anyone who isn't already in the lane.
songs.scout_note: Rap lane (Florida). Smallest pick: ~7.8K Spotify monthly listeners. Out Oct 19, 2026. Source: https://idontknowerik.substack.com/p/weekly-wrap-up-oct-26th-2026-nov. Thin evidence of buzz; unclear if solo or group. Spotify verified by fetch.

songs.title: openinghearts
songs.verdict: Surf Gang's South Florida chaos duo build a Euro-trance anthem, then let static tear it apart.
songs.body:
B0YG1RL, the duo of June Vinette and Angela Rio, make loud, chaotic music where dance, rap and hyperpop collide. "openinghearts" is half of the new wave double single (with "i dont recall"), produced by Surf Gang's 4evr, with a video shot in New York by Cass Morrison. It follows their EXIT 2B EP with Novagang and a self-titled album in October.

**Melody & hook:** the frame is Euro-trance, big and anthemic. **Production:** the twist is that it's swarmed by static and white noise, which Stereogum framed as an anthem under alien attack. **Vocals & delivery:** blown out to match.

For fans of the lane this is the sound sharpening. The knock: distortion as a concept can wear thin, and the trance bones need to carry it once the shock fades.
songs.scout_note: Hyperpop lane. Stereogum Nov 9, 2026: https://stereogum.com/2517160/b0yg1rl-i-dont-recall-openinghearts/music ; FADER feature May 2026. ~44K Spotify monthly listeners, indie label. YouTube verified via oEmbed (B0YG1RL channel). Also dropped a self-titled album Oct 1 and the single 'MOND LAN FINI' Sep 17 (https://open.spotify.com/track/2J5vKGVQ05dpdadZwDvEid) if you'd rather review those.

songs.title: Alternative Rock Music
songs.verdict: A name-your-price dariacore flip from a New Jersey producer the scene's own chroniclers keep naming.
songs.body:
ta1lsd0ll is a New Jersey producer in the dariacore/hyperflip scene, best known for a Sonic-themed release series. “Alternative Rock Music” is a name-your-price Bandcamp single out Sep 18, tagged electronic, experimental and samples.

**Hook:** dariacore lives on fast, meme-ready flips of familiar songs; which samples this one uses isn't documented, so name them after listening. **Sound design:** expect the scene's mashup chaos, high tempo and hyperpop sheen. **Build & drop:** not described anywhere yet.

It has a handful of Bandcamp supporters and a fan upload on YouTube, nothing more. The knock: dariacore is built for the in-crowd, and a single flip rarely wins over anyone outside it.
songs.scout_note: Hyperpop lane (dariacore). Out Sep 18, 2026 per official Bandcamp (fetched; it links instagram.com/ta1lsd0ll). Very underground; not on Spotify/Apple. YouTube link is a fan upload on 'pibbs music emporium' (title confirmed via oEmbed), so prefer Bandcamp. Scene context: https://www.chsperiscope.com/ae/2026/02/17/a-deep-dive-into-the-dariacore-hyperflip-scene/

songs.title: (L)ove (I)s (F)or (E)veryone
songs.verdict: Seventeen tracks of club-ready electropop with an antifascist spine, made in a sleepless month after a big tour.
songs.body:
Mietze Conte is a Vienna-based electropop artist coming off festival sets at Way Out West and MAGMA and the 2026 mixtape wufwufwuf. (L)ove (I)s (F)or (E)veryone is pitched as an antifascist record about resisting hate and building something better, and he made it in one sleepless studio month after his biggest North American tour.

**Melody & hook:** lead single “painting on a monument” is a club track, born from frustration with statues honoring fascists. **Lyrics:** its idea is that slow, gentle change can crack something hard and show what’s softer underneath. “origami” looks back at his teenage years in the city. **Production:** “lavender” is a collaboration with Australian producer 1tbsp, and “origami” is flagged as a production detour from the rest.

For a club-first record, the ideas give it more weight than most. The limit: 17 tracks made in a month is a lot to keep sharp, and the press so far covers the announcement rather than the finished album.
songs.scout_note: Hyperpop lane. Out Oct 29, 2026, 17 tracks (Spotify fetched). Line of Best Fit announcement: https://www.thelineofbestfit.com/news/mietze-conte-announces-new-album-love-is-for-everyone. Indie (Sumoclic). CHECK LISTENER COUNT: she tours UK/EU festivals and could be over 100k. Apple/SoundCloud links unverified, left blank.

songs.title: New Pop Standard
songs.verdict: An early, three-minute standout from a 37-track hyperpop marathon by an artist who now headlines Zepp-size rooms in Tokyo.
songs.body:
lilbesh ramko is a cult name in Japan's hyperpop and digicore scene, now big enough to sell out LIQUIDROOM and play POP YOURS. “New Pop Standard” (3:03) is track 3 on Ramko Helvetica, his third album, released Oct 10 on NAWHGANG: 37 tracks and no guest features.

**Production:** the album is tagged hyperpop, digicore, glitch pop and jersey club, so expect a maximal, chopped-up sound. **Melody & hook:** the title suggests a pop statement, and it comes early in the sequence. **Vocals & Lyrics:** no write-up covers this track in detail; listen for how the vocal sits in the mix.

The Dec 3 headline show at Zepp DiverCity, his biggest yet, says the audience is there. The knock: buried in a 37-track album with no single push, it has to earn its place, and the glitch-pop lane can wear thin for outsiders.
songs.scout_note: Hyperpop lane. Out Oct 10, 2026 (Spotify track fetched; album https://open.spotify.com/album/44yRfLuIoWA3ia9hHeNdPO). Source: idontknowerik.substack.com Sep 28-Oct 4 wrap-up. No label info or listener count; may be bigger than the others, check. CHECK SIZE: sizeable Japanese act (Zepp DiverCity headline Dec 3).

songs.title: universal will
songs.verdict: A three-minute closer to katie dey's most rock-leaning album yet, a bedroom-made concept record about tech and identity.
songs.body:
katie dey is a Melbourne cult name whose warped, pitched-voice bedroom pop has a devoted following. universal will, her seventh album and third self-released, came out Nov 6. She calls it an indie rock concept album about technology, social media, AI and identity, drawing on '90s alt-rock, recorded alone in her bedroom over about a year and a half. The title track closes it at 3:01.

**Production:** lead single "for you" swapped her glitchy palette for heavy drums and electric guitar, and the album is tagged shoegaze and noise rock alongside electronic. **Lyrics:** her imagery tends toward the vivid and unsettling. No source describes this specific track yet.

The album context is strong and her catalog earns trust. What the listen has to settle is whether the closer lands as a payoff or just a short coda.
songs.scout_note: Hyperpop-adjacent lane. Album out Nov 6, 2026; Stereogum announcement: https://stereogum.com/2514199/katie-dey-announces-new-album-universal-will-hear-for-you/music. YouTube lyric video on her official channel, confirmed via oEmbed (from 50percenthipster's Nov 6 NMF). Bandcamp link is the album page, taken from Stereogum. Veteran cult act rather than a new name; listener count unverified but likely small.

songs.title: r u?
songs.verdict: A small, yearning voice that lands like a powerful whisper, and the reason COLORS and FADER moved fast.
songs.body:
nomi. is a North Carolina-raised singer, songwriter and producer on Earth Angel Records, and “r u?” comes from her debut album this wolf may cry, produced with Zach Ezzy and Adam Krevlin. It got a COLORS show days before release and a FADER “Songs You Need” slot.

**Vocals & delivery:** FADER calls her voice tiny in tone but mighty, sung like a powerful whisper. **Lyrics:** COLORS frames it as sitting between letting go and holding on. **Production:** described as soulful and introspective; the studio version may differ from the stripped COLORS take.

Early singles drew support from names like Tyler, The Creator, SZA and Kaytranada, so the buzz is real even at a few thousand plays. The knock: quiet, yearning R&B is a crowded room, and a whisper needs a hook that stays.
songs.scout_note: R&B lane. Studio track out Oct 30, 2026 (Spotify fetched). COLORS show Oct 26; FADER 'Songs You Need' Oct 28: https://www.thefader.com/2026/10/28/songs-you-need-in-your-life-october-28-2026. Very small (Audiomack ~5K plays). YouTube link is the COLORS performance embedded on FADER, not the studio version.

songs.title: Way Back To You
songs.verdict: Thea Gustafsson builds a song about longing from drums and chopped-up vocals, and lets it stay a little unruly.
songs.body:
Becky and the Birds is Swedish singer-producer Thea Gustafsson, a longtime name in left-of-center pop with R&B roots. “Way Back To You” came out of California sessions with longtime collaborator Nick Velez. Stereogum covered it and it made Line of Best Fit’s discovery list.

**Production:** she started from the drums and built everything around how they felt, collaging rhythm with cut-up vocal samples. She says she wanted it lively, a bit unpredictable and messy in a good way. **Lyrics:** about longing for something out of reach while you keep moving toward it. **Vocals & delivery:** the voice works as sampled texture as much as lead. Ellen Nielsen directed two minimalist videos.

The collage approach should reward repeat listens. The knock: deliberate messiness can read as a sketch, and listeners who want her smoother side may find this harder to settle into.
songs.scout_note: R&B lane. Stereogum Nov 6, 2026: https://stereogum.com/2516783/becky-and-the-birds-way-back-to-you/music (video embedded there). Also on Line of Best Fit's New Music Discovery, Nov 6. CHECK LISTENER COUNT and label: established in alt-R&B circles, could be near 100k. No Spotify link verified.

songs.title: Love's Arp
songs.verdict: Dawuna breaks '90s R&B and glitchy neo-soul into eerie, spiritual songs about love, and Bandcamp Daily is right to rave.
songs.body:
Dawuna is Baltimore's Ian Mugerwa, who wrote and produced Love's Arp at home. It's his first album for True Panther: 13 songs about love in its romantic, spiritual and family forms, drawn from Diasporic Black music, old and new.

**Production:** Bandcamp Daily hears '90s R&B and glitchy neo-soul pulled apart into craggy, ghostly spirituals, with gospel harmonies behind and East African percussion rattling through; Heba Kadry mastered it. **Vocals & delivery:** on “Be Careful II”, a bass-heavy, sensual cut, his strained falsetto carries both love and the fear of losing it. **Lyrics:** anxiety shadows every kind of love here.

Called a generational talent in an Essential Releases pick, with Sly Stone, Prince and D'Angelo as reference points. The knock: it's built to unsettle, and the deliberate strain and tangled ending won't suit anyone after smooth R&B.
songs.scout_note: R&B/neo-soul lane. Bandcamp Daily Essential Releases Nov 6, 2026: https://daily.bandcamp.com/essential-releases/essential-releases-november-6-2026 (highlights 'Be Careful II'). Apple album fetched: Nov 6, 2026, True Panther (indie), 13 tracks. Listener count unknown, likely small.

songs.title: Playtime
songs.verdict: A '90s-leaning R&B love story from a Young Fyre production, with the singing out front.
songs.body:
Crystal Tamar is an independent R&B singer, and "Playtime" (out Oct 23) is built on her own story: meeting her husband in a way she never expected. She co-wrote it with songwriter Corey Mekell, and Grammy-winning producer Young Fyre (Bad Bunny, Lil Wayne, Kehlani) handled the beat.

**Vocals & delivery:** EARMILK called it some of her strongest singing yet. **Production** leans into classic, '90s-style R&B rather than modern trap-soul. **Lyrics:** love upending what you thought you wanted.

The credits are a step up for an indie singer, and the throwback lane suits slow-burn replays. The knock: '90s homage is a crowded space, so the listen has to find what's hers beyond the reference.
songs.scout_note: R&B lane. Out Oct 23, 2026 (Spotify fetched). Found via an EARMILK post dated Nov 2, 2026. Thin background info; check listener count and bio.

songs.title: Over
songs.verdict: A speed dembow and tribal techno specialist tries dubstep for the first time, and builds it for the soundsystem.
songs.body:
Amor Satyr is a Paris producer from the DIY bass scene, co-founder of WAJANG with Siu Mata, co-coiner of “speed dembow”, with records on SSPB and TraTraTrax and sets at Sónar and RA. “Over” (4:15) opens Judder Vinyl Series Vol. 2 and is his first dubstep track; Mixmag premiered it.

**Sound design:** Judder pitches the comp as raw, bass-weighted and soundsystem-first. **Groove:** the label says he carries his own energy onto dubstep's foundations rather than playing it straight. **Hook** and **Build & drop:** not described in any source; check how the drop lands on a real system.

As a 12-inch opener from a DJ with this pedigree, it has club life built in. The knock: a first try at a genre with fixed rules, and away from big speakers dubstep can lose most of its point.
songs.scout_note: Left-field electronic lane. Mixmag premiere Oct 4, 2026 (SoundCloud embed): https://mixmag.net/read/new-music-on-our-radar-this-week-blackhaine-horsegiirl-dj-heartstring-news. Judder Bandcamp: released Oct 23, 2026. SoundCloud upload is Mixmag's account, not the artist's. Club-circuit DJ, well under 100k.

songs.title: PLAYTHEDRUMS
songs.verdict: A bedroom-pop poet heads for the club with an ’80s-tinted opener that’s kitschy on purpose.
songs.body:
Skateland is Dorian Williams II, Las Vegas-raised and New York-based, who has shared stages with Foster the People, Major Lazer and Two Door Cinema Club. “PLAYTHEDRUMS” opens the six-track EP Ultra Kitsch, his turn away from serious-poet mode toward something closer to Vegas: neon, goofy and unserious.

**Melody & hook:** he says it was written for the clubs, and press describes an ’80s-tinged track that keeps adding layers. **Production:** the EP is built on watery bass, calm synths and airy vocals, mixing dream pop, art pop and indie electronica. **Vocals & delivery:** airy and blended into the atmosphere rather than out front.

As a mood piece for a dance floor it has a clear purpose. The limit: dreamy and club-ready pull in opposite directions, and coverage stays at roundup level, so whether it hits harder than pleasant is still open.
songs.scout_note: Indie/bedroom pop lane. Atwood Weekly Roundup Nov 6, 2026 (YouTube embed): https://atwoodmagazine.com/?p=231598 ; Melodic Magazine Nov 2 (source of IG): https://www.melodicmag.com/news/new-music/skateland-finds-the-happy-medium-between-past-and-future-nostalgia-on-visceral-ep-ultra-kitsch/. Exact release date not confirmed (coverage starts Nov 2). Listener count unknown, likely small.
